title: Write a GitLab CI Pipeline: Test, Build, and a Gated Deploy
intro: The GitHub Actions labs have their GitLab counterpart here. Write the .gitlab-ci.yml for a Python service: tests on every push, an image build on main only, and a production deploy that waits for a person.

steps.hint:
Top level: 'stages:' as a list, then one mapping per job. A job:
  unit:
    stage: test
    image: python:3.12
    cache:
      key:
        files:
          - requirements.txt
      paths:
        - .cache/pip
    script:
      - pip install -r requirements.txt
      - pytest
Rules:
    rules:
      - if: $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH == "main"
        when: manual
The environment can be written 'environment: production' or with a name: key.
steps.solution:
stages:
  - test
  - build
  - deploy

unit:
  stage: test
  image: python:3.12
  cache:
    key:
      files:
        - requirements.txt
    paths:
      - .cache/pip
  script:
    - pip install -r requirements.txt
    - pytest

image:
  stage: build
  image: gcr.io/kaniko-project/executor:debug
  script:
    - /kaniko/executor --context $CI_PROJECT_DIR --destination $CI_REGISTRY_IMAGE:$CI_COMMIT_SHORT_SHA
  rules:
    - if: $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH == "main"

production:
  stage: deploy
  script:
    - ./deploy.sh $CI_COMMIT_SHORT_SHA
  environment:
    name: production
  needs:
    - image
  rules:
    - if: $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH == "main"
      when: manual
steps.explanation: Tests on every push; an image tagged with the commit, built on main; and a production deploy of that same commit that waits for a click.
steps.why: The choices that matter. The cache key is the hash of requirements.txt, so the cache is reused until dependencies change and never serves stale packages afterwards. The image is built with Kaniko, which needs no Docker daemon and no privileged runner, unlike docker:dind (cicd-tutorial-016). It's tagged with the commit SHA, never 'latest', so the deploy job installs exactly the image that was built in this pipeline (cicd-incident-005). 'rules' replace the older only/except and decide whether a job exists in a pipeline at all: on a feature branch, this pipeline contains only the test job. 'needs' ties the deploy to the build job explicitly. 'when: manual' puts a person in front of production, and the environment name lets GitLab record deployments, restrict who may run them, and offer rollback. Protect the main branch and scope the deploy credentials to the production environment, or a job on any branch could read them.
